title: Sentinel-1 SAR Data Access — Copernicus Data Space
content:
Sentinel-1 is a C-band SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite constellation operated by ESA as part of the Copernicus programme. It provides all-weather, day-and-night radar imaging, making it exceptionally valuable for disaster monitoring including floods, earthquakes, and landslides.

For flood mapping, Sentinel-1 backscatter values over flooded areas are significantly lower than over dry land due to specular reflection of radar signals off smooth water surfaces. Change detection between pre-event and post-event SAR images allows automated delineation of flood extents with high spatial resolution (10 m GRD products).

The Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem provides free and open access to Sentinel-1 data through multiple APIs including OData, STAC, and SentinelHub. Authentication uses OAuth2 client credentials. Data is available in IW (Interferometric Wide) swath mode for most land applications, with Level-1 GRD and SLC products suitable for flood mapping and change detection respectively.

title: GDACS Alert: Major Flood Event — Bangladesh
content:
GDACS ALERT — RED LEVEL: Major Flood in Bangladesh

A severe monsoon flood event is affecting northeastern Bangladesh, particularly the Sylhet and Sunamganj districts. The Surma and Kushiyara rivers have exceeded danger levels by 2-3 metres. Approximately 4 million people are estimated to be affected.

Flash floods triggered by extremely heavy rainfall (>300 mm in 48 hours) have inundated over 800,000 hectares of agricultural land. Road networks in the affected districts are severely disrupted. Emergency response operations are ongoing by the Bangladesh Disaster Management Authority (BDMA) in coordination with UN agencies.

Satellite change detection using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery (pre-event: June 1, post-event: June 16) shows a flood footprint of approximately 180,000 hectares in the Sylhet division. The Copernicus Emergency Management Service has been activated.

title: Turkey-Syria Earthquake 2023 — Humanitarian Response Situation Report
content:
Situation Report #12 — Turkey-Syria Earthquake Response

On 6 February 2023, two devastating earthquakes of magnitude Mw 7.8 and Mw 7.5 struck southeast Turkey and northern Syria, causing widespread destruction across 11 provinces. The earthquakes are among the deadliest in the region's recorded history.

Key figures: Over 50,000 confirmed fatalities in Turkey alone. More than 100,000 people injured. Approximately 13.5 million people affected across both countries. 14 provinces declared disaster zones in Turkey.

Satellite imagery analysis: The Copernicus Emergency Management Service activated the EMSN (Emergency Management Service - Mapping) for affected areas. Sentinel-1 SAR change detection identified over 12,000 collapsed or heavily damaged structures in Kahramanmaras, Hatay, and Gaziantep provinces. Coherence change detection highlighted areas of ground deformation along the East Anatolian Fault.

Search and rescue operations involved teams from 94 countries. Humanitarian needs include emergency shelter, water, food, and medical care for an estimated 1.5 million displaced people.

title: Google Earth Engine — SAR Change Detection Guide
content:
SAR Basics in Google Earth Engine

Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data in Google Earth Engine is primarily sourced from the Sentinel-1 mission. The Sentinel-1 GRD (Ground Range Detected) collection is available as ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S1_GRD') and includes data from 2014 onwards.

Key SAR processing concepts for disaster mapping:
1. Backscatter change detection: Compare pre- and post-event VV or VH polarisation backscatter.    Flooded areas show reduced backscatter; building collapse may show increased or changed backscatter.
2. Coherence analysis: Phase coherence between two SAR acquisitions drops to near zero over flooded    or disturbed surfaces, providing a sensitive change indicator.
3. Filtering: Lee, Gamma-MAP, or refined Lee filters reduce speckle noise in SAR imagery.

Example flood mapping workflow in GEE:
- Filter Sentinel-1 collection by date, orbit direction (ASCENDING/DESCENDING), and instrument mode (IW).
- Select VV polarisation for open water detection.
- Apply otsu thresholding on the difference image (post - pre) to classify flood pixels.
- Mask permanent water bodies using the JRC Global Surface Water dataset.

Earth Engine scales analysis across Google's infrastructure, making it suitable for regional and national-scale flood mapping during active disaster events.

title: NASA Earthdata — Disaster Applications and Rapid Response
content:
NASA Earthdata Disasters Program

NASA provides near-real-time Earth observation data to support disaster response and recovery. Key datasets relevant to disaster intelligence include:

MODIS (Terra/Aqua): Daily global coverage at 250m–1km resolution. FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) provides near-real-time active fire detections. Useful for wildfire monitoring and flood inundation mapping.

Landsat 8/9: 30-metre multispectral imagery with 16-day revisit. Critical for change detection over agricultural areas, urban damage assessment, and pre/post disaster comparisons.

ARIA (Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis) Project: Provides processed SAR-based damage proxy maps within 24-48 hours of major earthquakes and other disasters. Uses Sentinel-1 and ALOS-2 SAR data. Products include Damage Proxy Maps (DPM) showing likely building damage extent.

IMERG (Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM): Near-real-time precipitation data at 0.1-degree resolution, updated every 30 minutes. Essential for flood triggering analysis and rainfall-triggered landslide assessments.

All NASA Earthdata products are freely available through Earthdata Search. API access is available through CMR (Common Metadata Repository) and OPeNDAP.

title: Cyclone Mocha — Myanmar and Bangladesh Landfall Report
content:
Cyclone Mocha Situation Report #3 — Myanmar / Bangladesh

Cyclone Mocha made landfall near Sittwe, Rakhine State, Myanmar on 14 May 2023 with maximum sustained winds of 209 km/h (Category 4 equivalent), making it one of the strongest cyclones ever recorded in the Bay of Bengal region.

Impact summary:
- Rakhine State: Approximately 800,000 people affected. Sittwe city sustained catastrophic damage   with over 80% of structures reported damaged or destroyed. Massive displacement of Rohingya   communities from IDP camps.
- Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh: 300,000 people in Rohingya refugee camps affected by strong winds   and heavy rainfall. 70,000+ shelters damaged.

Satellite analysis: Copernicus EMS activated. Sentinel-1 SAR imagery acquired on 15 May showed extensive inundation along the Kaladan River delta and coastal storm surge flooding extending 10-15 km inland. Damage assessments conducted using Pleiades and WorldView optical imagery in combination with SAR change detection.
